text.v: Rust knows that we didn’t cover every possible case and even knows which pattern we forgot! Matches in Rust are
: We must exhaust every last possibility in order for the code to be valid. Especially in the case of
, when Rust prevents us from forgetting to explicitly handle the
case, it protects us from assuming that we have a value when we might have null, thus making the billion-dollar mistake discussed earlier impossible.

Using enums, we can also take special actions for a few particular values, but for all other values take one default action. Imagine we’re implementing a game where, if you roll a 3 on a dice roll, your player doesn’t move but instead gets a fancy new hat. If you roll a 7, your player loses a fancy hat.
